To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we present an approach for online modeling and probabilistic querying of streaming data, (2) we present a novel approach for online filtering and probabilistic modeling using particle filters, and (3) we present an implementation of our approach and demonstrate its feasibility and advantages.

(1) we propose an efficient system for real-time application of probabilistic models to streams, (2) we show that our system is capable of processing complex queries over probabilistic data, (3) we present an efficient implementation of particle filters that is tightly integrated with a relational DBMS.

(1) We present a novel system for online modeling of streaming relational data using dynamic probabilistic models, (2) We present a declarative language for specifying dynamic probabilistic models in the context of a relational database system, (3) We present novel techniques for efficient processing of queries on probabilistic model-based views using a particle-based representation of the model, (4) We demonstrate the effectiveness of our system using a number of synthetic and real datasets.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of extending the relational model to facilitate efficient real- time application of dynamic probabilistics models to streaming data, in particular to enable online probabilistic modeling of streaming data, and to enable efficient querying of such models.
the design, implementation and analysis of a system for real-time processing of data streams.
the development of a system that enables the online processing of streaming data, using probabilistic models, and the efficient querying and analysis of the results of the model.

we have presented the first system for online modeling of streaming databases, and demonstrated the feasibility of this approach.
we have presented a novel approach to the integration of dynamic probabilistic modeling with relational databases, that enables the efficient processing of queries over probabilistic data.
our system provides a practical framework for online modeling of streaming relational data, that is able to efficiently process a wide range of probabilistic queries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed system is capable of efficiently applying dynamic probabilistic models over streaming data, and that it can be used for online probabilistic modeling and filtering, and that it supports efficient probabilistic querying of the resulting probabilistic database.

The main takeaway from our work is that

probabilistic modeling of streaming data is a promising approach for a variety of real-time applications, and that the tight coupling of probabilistic models to databases can lead to highly efficient and scalable systems for such applications.
probabilistic models can be integrated into a DBMS and applied in a streaming fashion, without requiring any changes in the DBMS itself.
